source.repro: Capture perBaseLetter on volvox_alignments at ctgA:1..1,000 / 1..4,000 / 1..48,000 under `--backend=all --skip-webgpu --swiftshader -u` from products/jbrowse-web, then histogram each targeted capture. `pure palette` is the share of inked pixels within 2 per channel of one of the five base colours the mode draws (Material red/blue/green/orange/grey); `distinct` counts every distinct RGB triple. The scenes are not in the tree — see the repro on per-base-cross-backend-drift for how to stand them up.
source.notes: The purity column is the test of a mechanism claim, not a quality score. PER_BASE_SUBPIXEL_BIN.md explains the sub-pixel bin's visible effect by saying both backends floor a cell to 1 CSS px and blend what overlaps, so a pixel under N cells reports roughly their mean. Canvas2D does that. The GPU does not: it holds 160-269 distinct colours and stays majority-pure at every zoom measured, because `pileupCellX` snaps each cell to a whole pixel column and the winning cell covers it outright. Its impurity is edge antialiasing at cell boundaries, which is why it is WORST at 0.8 bp/px where cells are ~1.27px and land mid-column, rather than at the widest zoom where the most cells compete. No before-the-bin arm was captured, so this does not touch the bin's own before/after appearance measurement — it bounds the mechanism sentence attached to it.
